lead: A subagent does the noisy part in its own context window and returns only the summary. It's worth what doesn't come back: logs, searches, and files the main conversation will never read again. In this lesson you write a read-only subagent with a return of up to 12 lines and actually check the size of what came back.
objetivo: create a read-only subagent with a return of up to 12 lines and check that its answer fits in the main conversation.

aprende.t: What the subagent receives and what it returns
The .claude/agents/[nome].md file and the fields that matter
Restricted tools: what the list locks and what only the instruction asks for
Fixed-format return with a confidence line

hero_alt: Main circuit board connected by a short cable to a smaller board in its own shielded box.

secoes.sub: Behavior of Claude Code 2.1.303, from the official docs read on 10/19/2026. Click each step.

nos.detalhe: Use the main conversation when there is back-and-forth, when the phases share a lot of context (planning, implementing, testing), for a quick change, or when latency matters: a subagent that isn't a fork starts from zero and takes time to get its bearings.

itens.t: the task message written by Claude

nos.detalhe: The subagent doesn't receive the Claude Code system prompt or the conversation history. It receives the prompt from its own file, the task message, the CLAUDE.md hierarchy (except Explore and Plan, or with omitClaudeMd), and a snapshot of git status. That's why the request needs to cite paths, not paste content.

It runs with its own context, tools, and permissions, and counts against the same usage limit of your subscription. It can open its own subagents up to three layers below the conversation by default; CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH=1 turns off nesting (the operating limit of the lesson 1 kit is one level). With 20 running at the same time, the 21st is refused.

Only the final answer goes back to the conversation. Many subagents with detailed returns fill the context just the same: Anthropic recommends condensed summaries of about 1,000 to 2,000 tokens (context engineering post, 09/29/2025). Ask for structured data, not narrative.

secoes.volta: Need another step? The conversation passes the summary to the next subagent (chaining)
secoes.legenda: Fork is something else: it inherits the whole conversation (/subtask) and loses input isolation. Good for a side task that needs what has already been said.

secoes.sub: Of the supported frontmatter, four change behavior day to day.

texto: Claude delegates when the task matches the description. Write when to use it and when not to use it, in one sentence.
A new file in .claude/agents/ takes effect without restarting, except when the agents/ folder didn't exist at the start of the session.
List of tools it can use. Without the field, it inherits the conversation's tools. Without Write, Edit and Bash, it writes nothing, no matter how much the model wants to.
disallowedTools with a specifier, like Bash(git push *), removes the whole tool; to block only that command, use permissions.deny.
Accepts an alias or inherit. Choose by the role's level (lesson 7), not by the name of the day: names change.
The runtime kit uses opus, sonnet and haiku in the three roles; treat that as an example of different levels.
The body of the file becomes the system prompt. Put the response format in it: maximum number of lines, path:line as proof, and a final confidence line.
This format lets the orchestrator read 10 summaries without filling its own window.

secoes.sub: Create the file, check the fields without spending quota, then make a real call.

blocos.conteudo:
---
name: explorador
description: Searches the project and returns only a summary. Use it to sweep many files without filling the main conversation.
tools: Read, Grep, Glob
model: inherit
---
You are the explorer. Change nothing.
Return at most 12 lines:
1. The answer in one sentence.
2. Up to 8 lines in the format path:line — what is there.
3. Last line: CONFIANÇA alta|média|baixa and what you did not check.

blocos.rot: Terminal · no-quota rehearsal: check the project's subagents
blocos.conteudo:
cd ~/treino-multi
python3 - .claude/agents/*.md <<'PY'
import sys, re
for f in sys.argv[1:]:
    m = re.match(r"---\n(.*?)\n---", open(f, encoding="utf-8").read(), re.S)
    if not m:
        print(f, "→ SEM frontmatter"); continue
    d = {k.strip(): v.strip() for k, v in (l.split(":", 1) for l in m.group(1).splitlines() if ":" in l)}
    tools = d.get("tools", "(herda todas)")
    escreve = "tools" not in d or any(x in tools for x in ("Write", "Edit", "Bash"))
    print(f"{d.get('name', '?')} · tools: {tools} · model: {d.get('model', '(herda)')} · escreve: {'sim' if escreve else 'não'}")
PY

blocos.rot: Terminal · real call (uses a little quota)
blocos.conteudo:
cd ~/treino-multi
claude -p "Use o subagente explorador para descobrir onde este projeto define a própria versão e quais arquivos citam essa versão. Repita apenas o resumo que ele devolver, sem comentar." < /dev/null > resposta.md
grep -c "^CONFIANÇA" resposta.md; wc -l < resposta.md

abas.html:
## conferidor (sem cota)
executor · tools: Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob · model: sonnet · escreve: sim
explorador · tools: Read, Grep, Glob · model: inherit · escreve: não
planejador · tools: Read, Grep, Glob · model: opus · escreve: não
revisor · tools: Read, Bash, Grep, Glob · model: haiku · escreve: sim

## resposta.md (chamada real, 29 s)
A versão é 0.3.0 e a fonte da verdade é o arquivo VERSION na raiz. Não existe package.json nem pyproject, e nenhuma constante no código define a versão. Ela também aparece em mais 6 arquivos, num total de 9 ocorrências:

- `VERSION:1`: `0.3.0` (definição)
- `CHANGELOG.md:3`: `## 0.3.0 — 2026-10-05`
- `runtime/mods/runtime-guarda/.claude-plugin/plugin.json:3`: `"version": "0.3.0"`
- `runtime/mods/runtime-painel/.claude-plugin/plugin.json:3`: `"version": "0.3.0"`
- `guia/index.html:329` e `:335`: rótulo "Fase 3 · 0.3.0" e rodapé "INEMA Agent Runtime 0.3.0"
(… guia/en e guia/es, as mesmas duas citações …)

CONFIANÇA alta. Não conferi o que o .gitignore exclui nem os outros números de versão (0.1.0, 0.2.0), e não verifiquei se algum script lê o VERSION.

The ## headings separate the two rounds. Declared cuts: two lines of the translated guide and a final line that the global CLAUDE.md of the capture machine adds. On your machine, wc -l should be between 10 and 15.

The checker marked revisor · … · escreve: sim. The kit file says "Não altere arquivos", but the tool list includes Bash, and Bash writes. The instruction is a request to the model; the tool list is the lock.

revisor · tools: Read, Bash, Grep, Glob · model: haiku · escreve: sim

The reviewer needs Bash to run the criteria. To keep it from actually writing, the way out is sandbox (lesson 5) or a permission rule; guarding against deleting and writing is covered in course 4. And the real call without < /dev/null waits 3 s for stdin and warns: Warning: no stdin data received in 3s.

secoes.sub: The rehearsal checks the file; the real call checks the return.

exercicios.texto: Create .claude/agents/explorador.md in the training project and run the checker.
exercicios.pronto: the checker prints explorador · tools: Read, Grep, Glob · model: inherit · escreve: não.

exercicios.texto: Make the real call. Then swap the question for one from your real project, with the same subagent.
exercicios.pronto: grep -c "^CONFIANÇA" resposta.md → 1 and wc -l < resposta.md → at most 15, on both questions.

perguntas.p: What comes back from the subagent to the main conversation?
perguntas.explica: Only the final answer comes back. That's why the return format, written in the body of the file, is the most important part.

perguntas.p: Does the subagent receive the main conversation's history?
opcoes: Only if the agent file has model: inherit, which makes it inherit the model and the whole conversation
No: it gets its own prompt, the task, the CLAUDE.md and the git status; the fork is what inherits
perguntas.explica: A regular subagent starts clean. The fork inherits the whole conversation, and in doing so loses input isolation.

perguntas.p: A reviewer has tools: Read, Bash, Grep, Glob and the instruction "don't change files". Can it write?
opcoes: Yes: Bash writes; the instruction is a request, the tool list is the lock
No, because Write and Edit aren't on the list, and without them there's no way to save a file
perguntas.explica: With Bash it can write using echo, sed, or rm. To really lock it down: sandbox (lesson 5) or a permission rule (course 4).

perguntas.p: When is it NOT worth delegating to a subagent?
opcoes: A task with a lot of back and forth and phases that share the same context
Self-contained work whose result fits in a short summary for the main conversation
A search that generates a lot of logs
perguntas.explica: Back and forth and shared context stay in the main conversation; the subagent starts from scratch and would have to reread everything.

itens.t: Worth it for what doesn't come back
itens.texto: Logs, searches, and files stay in the subagent's window; only the summary comes back.
Read, Grep, Glob don't write; Bash does, no matter what the instruction says.
Maximum lines, path:line as proof, and a confidence line, written in the body of the file.
